holdings.name: Chevron
holdings.note: Valuation 2026-11-09 @ $212.61, valued at $70 Brent (mid-cycle), not today's ~$97. Base ~$160 = avg of 15x × mid-cycle 2027 EPS ~$8.9 ($134; 2025 adj. ~$7.4 + >10 %/yr plan) and Gordon on mid-cycle FCF/sh ~$11, g 2 % ($187). Cyclical → 35 % off = $105 (≈6.8 % yield on $7.12). Bear $66 = $5.5 EPS at $55 Brent × 12x. Reverse DCF: today's price assumes roughly $85–90 Brent for years. Watch flag 'FCF/sh −23 %/yr since 2022' = 2022 oil peak, not a business problem.
holdings.thesis: Integrated major with Hess (Guyana) + Permian + TCO. Plan to 2030 at $70 Brent: FCF and EPS >10 %/yr, capex $18–21bn, capex+dividend breakeven <$50, buybacks $10–20bn/yr. Own it for the dividend; add only when the oil price puts it on sale.
holdings.bull: Q3 26: adj. EPS $5.28, adj. FCF $14.2bn, net debt −$7.8bn in the quarter; record US refining. Venezuela, data-centre power (2027) and $3–4bn cost cuts as extra levers. 35+ yrs of dividend raises.
holdings.bear: Earnings are riding ~$97 Brent (Middle East conflict) — adj. EPS fell 13 % q/q when Brent slipped $104→97. Underlying production shrank y/y once Hess was lapped. At $70 Brent the stock is ~24x mid-cycle EPS. US 15 % WHT credited.
holdings.kill: I'm wrong if FCF at ~$70 Brent stays under $15bn (≈ dividend + minimal buyback), the dividend isn't raised in Jan, or net debt/EBITDA goes above 1.5x without a big deal.

holdings.name: Allianz
holdings.note: Valuation 2026-11-09 @ €451.10. Base ~€490 = avg of 12.4x (own 2021–25 median P/E) × 2027e EPS ~€34 (€422) and Gordon on earnings: €34 × 82 % payout (g 3 %, RoE 17 %) / 5 % = €560. Average uncertainty → 25 % off = €370 (≈5 % yield on 2026e div ~€19). Bear €225 = €25 EPS × 9x. Reverse DCF: at 8 % hurdle today's price needs only ~1 %/yr growth — cheap on my hurdle, rich vs its own multiple (market uses ~10 % CoE).
holdings.thesis: Diversified primary insurer + PIMCO/AGI. Core EPS H1 26 €16.44 (+17.5 %, +10 % adj.), core RoE 20.7 %, Solvency II 225 % (highest since 2018). 2026 op. profit target €17.4bn ±1bn; 60 % payout + buybacks. Add when the multiple falls back to ~11x.
holdings.bull: EPS target +7–9 %/yr 2025–27 and running above it; dividend €17.10 (+11 %) with €2.5bn buyback; asset management record inflows (€84bn H1). Capital surplus allows more buybacks.
holdings.bear: Stock re-rated from ~11x to ~14x trailing; yield 3.8 % vs 4.7 % 5-yr avg. Motor margins thin (GDV), nat-cat year or a bond-market shock hits PIMCO flows + book value. German stock, no foreign WHT (26.4 % Abgeltungsteuer only).
holdings.kill: I'm wrong if core EPS growth falls below 5 % two years running, Solvency II drops under 180 %, or the dividend is held flat.

holdings.name: Munich Re
holdings.note: Valuation 2026-11-09 @ €569.20. Base ~€700 = avg of 11.5x × normalised EPS €50 (2026 target €6.3bn with budgeted major losses / ~126m sh) = €575 and Gordon on earnings: €50 × 82 % payout (g 3 %, RoE 17 %) / 5 % = €824. Cyclical (soft reinsurance market) → 35 % off = €455 (≈6 % yield on ~€27.5 2026e div). Bear €270 = €30 EPS (heavy cat year + soft pricing) × 9x. Reverse DCF: at 8 % hurdle price implies ~−1.6 %/yr; market prices ~11–13 % CoE (Jefferies 13 %). Old Radar card had buy < €535.
holdings.thesis: World's #1 reinsurer + ERGO primary. 2026 net profit guide raised to €6.6bn (9M €5.7bn) on very low major losses. Ambition 2030: RoE >18 %, EPS >8 %/yr. Dividend €24 (2025), ~€27.5 expected. Add only when the soft cycle is in the price.
holdings.bull: Diversified (ERGO, L&H re) cushions the P&C cycle; investment result up (5.5 % RoI Q2); reserve buffers; buybacks + 80 %-ish payout. Below-budget losses in 2026 fund reserves for 2027.
holdings.bear: Soft market deepening: cat rates −12–15 % at Jan 26, risk-adj. −5.5 % at July, S&P/Fitch expect 2027 declines as large as 2026; reinsurance revenue guide cut €40→38bn. 2026 profit leans on major losses at 4.9 % vs 18 % budget — not repeatable. No foreign WHT.
holdings.kill: I'm wrong if normalised EPS (with budgeted losses) falls below €45, P&C re combined ratio runs above 85 % in a normal-loss year, or the dividend isn't raised.

holdings.name: Johnson & Johnson
holdings.note: Valuation 2026-11-09 @ $276.22. Base ~$212 = avg of 16x × 2027e EPS ~$12.5 ($200) and Gordon on FCF/sh ~$9.0 next yr, g 4 %, 8 % hurdle ($225). Wide moat → 15 % off = $180 (≈3.0 % yield on $5.36). Bear $143 = $11 EPS × 13x (+ talc). Reverse DCF: $276 needs ~4.8 %/yr FCF growth forever at 8 %.
holdings.thesis: Pharma (Tremfya, Darzalex, Carvykti, ICOTYDE) + MedTech, AAA balance sheet, 60+ yrs of raises. 2026 guide: sales $101.2bn (+7.4 %), adj. EPS $11.10 after M&A charges. Great business at a full price (~25x fwd); add only on a de-rating.
holdings.bull: Innovative Medicine +7.7 % in Q3 despite Stelara biosimilars; pipeline wins (Rybrevant Faspro, ICOTYDE PsA); mgmt targets double-digit growth by end of decade; FCF ~$20bn covers $13bn dividends ~1.6x.
holdings.bear: Up from $185 to $276 in a year; yield 1.9 % vs 2.7 % 5-yr avg; ~25x fwd vs ~15–17x history. MedTech only +2.5 % op. growth; talc resolution charge (Q3 GAAP EPS $0.09); orthopaedics separation execution; US drug-pricing policy. US 15 % WHT credited.
holdings.kill: I'm wrong if adj. EPS growth stays below 4 % in 2027–28 ex deal costs, a talc deal needs a dividend freeze, or FCF falls below the dividend.

holdings.name: Realty Income
holdings.note: Valuation 2026-11-09 @ $59.04. Base ~$65 = avg of 14x × 2027e AFFO ~$4.58 ($64; history ~13x since 2022, ~17x before) and Gordon on dividend $3.29 next 12m, g 3 %, 8 % hurdle ($66). Net lease scale/cost-of-capital moat → 20 % off = $52 (≈6.3 % yield). Bear $48 = AFFO $4.40 × 11x (2023 low) — cushion only ~8 %, because the bear case is rates, not AFFO. Reverse DCF: at $59 the 5.5 % yield + 2.5 % growth = exactly 8 %.
holdings.thesis: Largest net-lease REIT, 98.8 % occupancy, 103.5 % rent recapture, 676 consecutive monthly dividends. 2026 AFFO guide $4.45–4.46 (+~4 %), $10bn investments at ~6.8–7.3 % cash yields. Income anchor; add when yield >6 %.
holdings.bull: AFFO growth steady through 2022–26 rate shock; private capital (KKR Europe JV) and credit investments add growth without equity; payout ~73 % of AFFO.
holdings.bear: ~$2.9bn of 2027 maturities at ~2.9 % refinance higher; Q4 guide implies AFFO dips to $1.10–1.11; net debt/EBITDA 5.4x; dividend growth only ~1 %/yr; equity issuance dilutes. REIT dividend: US 15 % WHT (credited), fully taxable in DE.
holdings.kill: I'm wrong if AFFO/share falls y/y, occupancy drops below 97 %, or new investments can't be made at a spread above the cost of capital for a full year.

holdings.name: Vanguard FTSE All-World High Dividend Yield (Dist)
Coca-Cola
holdings.note: Valuation 2026-11-09 @ $95.67. Base ~$80 = avg of 23x × 2027e EPS ~$3.55 ($82) and Gordon on FCF/sh ~$3.15 next yr, g 4 %, 8 % hurdle ($79). Wide moat → 15 % off = $68 (≈3.1 % yield on $2.12). Bear $57 = $3.00 EPS × 19x. Reverse DCF: $95.67 needs ~4.7 %/yr FCF growth forever. Red flag 'dividend > FCF 2024–25' is one-offs (2024 IRS deposit, 2025 $6.1bn Fairlife payment; FCF ex-Fairlife 2025 $11.4bn vs ~$8.8bn dividends).
holdings.thesis: Global concentrate franchise: ~33 % op. margin, value-share gains, 60+ yrs of dividend raises. 2026 guide raised 3x: comparable EPS ≥+11 %, organic rev ≥+5 %, FCF ≥$13bn. Add only well below fair value; at $95 it trades ~28x forward, a full price for 4–7 % EPS growth.
holdings.bull: Q3 26 volume +5 % (Zero Sugar +16 % in Q2), op. margin 33.4 %; FCF ≥$13bn ≈ $3.0/sh covers the $2.12 dividend ~1.4x once Fairlife/IRS one-offs are gone. Refranchising makes it more asset-light; buybacks resume.
holdings.bear: At $95.67 yield 2.2 % vs 2.8 % 5-yr avg; ~28x fwd on mid-single-digit growth = multiple risk (19x at $3.55 is $67). 2027: ~8 % revenue headwind from deals, FX turning, GLP-1/affordability, open IRS transfer-pricing case. US 15 % WHT is credited in DE, no loss.
holdings.kill: I'm wrong if organic growth drops below 4 % for 4 quarters or FCF ex one-offs falls below the dividend (~$9bn), or the IRS case is lost without a payment plan that leaves the dividend covered.
